# Task: sphinx issue #741 — autodoc inherited-members fails for inherited attributes (data members)

## Environment
- cwd: C:/Users/agent/work/work/sphinx-8548-nopanel
- Sphinx 3.4.0 dev checkout, git HEAD dd1615c59 ("Merge PR #8543")
- Tests: C:/Users/agent/work/projects/stack/campaign/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
- Constraint: fix in source only, NO test changes, NO commit, leave in working tree.

## Key code locations
- sphinx/ext/autodoc/importer.py: get_class_members() (line ~254) — builds members dict
  with ClassAttribute(subject, name, value, docstring). Docstrings for attributes come
  from analyzer.attr_docs keyed by (namespace, attrname) where namespace = '.'.join(objpath)
  i.e. the CURRENT class only (line ~310-316).
- sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py:
  - ClassDocumenter.get_object_members (line ~1586): with inherited-members, returns all
    members.values() incl. docstring=m.docstring.
  - Documenter.add_content (line ~587): looks up attr_docs with key =
    ('.'.join(objpath[:-1]), objpath[-1]) — again only current-class namespace.
  - filter_members (line ~654): (namespace, membername) in attr_docs check — same issue.

## Hypothesis (to verify)
When documenting a subclass with :inherited-members:, an attribute defined+documented in
the base class (doc-comment `#: ...` or `self.x = ...  #: ...`) is found as a member of
the subclass, but its docstring is NOT found because the analyzer lookup uses only the
subclass namespace, never the base class namespace. So the attribute shows up undocumented
(or is dropped when undoc-members is off).

## Next steps
1. Write a repro script: base class with documented attr, subclass, autoclass directive
   with :inherited-members:, check output lacks the docstring.
2. Fix: in get_class_members (and/or add_content/filter_members), walk the MRO and try
   (base_namespace, attrname) keys too.
3. Run relevant tests: tests/test_ext_autodoc.py, tests/test_ext_autodoc_configs.py.

## Regression found + fix plan (name_mangling)
My first importer edit set class_=subject on base-namespace INSTANCEATTR entries.
ClassDocumenter.get_object_members (non-inherited mode) keeps members where
m.class_ == self.object -> Bar (subclass of Foo) gained Foo.__name (attr_docs
('Foo','__name')) without :inherited-members: -> test_name_mangling broke
(6 failed vs 5 baseline).

not subject. Then non-inherited filter (class_ == self.object) excludes them
(old behavior preserved), inherited-members mode includes them with docstring.
Also REVERT the filter_members attr_doc_namespaces change (docstring now flows
via ObjectMember.docstring from importer; keep filter_members minimal).
Keep add_content MRO-keys fix (self.parent-based, objpath[:-2]+[cls.__name__]).
Then: repro + full test_ext_autodoc.py vs baseline (5 pre-existing failures:
special_members, enum_class, coroutine, TypeVar, test_autodoc).

## Root cause (confirmed by reading + repro)
get_class_members() (importer.py:310-316) only matches analyzer.attr_docs entries whose
namespace == '.'.join(objpath) — the CURRENT class. When documenting Derived with
:inherited-members:, attrs defined in Base have attr_docs keyed ('Base', 'attr1') /
('Base.attr2'...) — namespace never matches 'Derived', so:
  - attr1/attr2 get NO docstring -> ClassAttribute(..., docstring=None)
  - filter_members() drops members whose (namespace, name) not in attr_docs when
    they have no __doc__ -> members vanish entirely (repro showed empty output).
Same namespace-only lookup in Documenter.add_content (attr_docs[(ns, name)]).
